disclaimer: Reminder reference only - NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set by regulation and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources before hunting or trapping. Fur harvesting in Nova Scotia is governed by the Wildlife Act, R.S.N.S. 1989, c. 504 and the Fur Harvesting Regulations, N.S. Reg. 165/1987 (amended to N.S. Reg. 25/2026). This dataset is for the separate Canada clone of Opossum Foot; it is NOT part of the US app, which stays US-only and untouched.

license_summary.accidental_catch: A person who accidentally catches a fur-bearing animal they are not entitled to must forthwith release it alive, OR report it immediately to the Department before removing it from the trap site, OR complete an Accidental Harvest Form before removing it (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 11(12)). The 2026 Summary: report immediately to a local DNR office (office hours) or 1-800-565-2224 after hours, and complete the Accidental Harvest Form (booklet p. 57). One accidentally caught fisher's pelt may be kept (carcass turned in, pelt stamped); raccoons taken accidentally in fox/coyote sets before the raccoon season may be kept (ss. 6(6)-(7)).
license_summary.certified_traps: Body-gripping traps for beaver, fisher, raccoon, weasel, otter, lynx and bobcat may only be traps listed in Schedule A of the Fur Harvesting Regulations as certified killing traps for that species; muskrat body-grippers only underwater as submersion sets or, on land, if Schedule A-listed for muskrat (ss. 11(20)-(21)). Beaver restraining traps must be Schedule B-listed (s. 11(22)); foot-encapsulating traps for raccoon and leghold traps for lynx/bobcat must be Schedule B-listed restraining traps (s. 11(14)(d),(g)). The schedules are headed 'Certified under the Canadian Trap Certification Program' - the national AIHTS certification administered by the Fur Institute of Canada; the 2026 Summary directs trappers to fur.ca/certified-traps/ for the up-to-date list. See the 'aihts' section of this dataset.
license_summary.course: Furharvester Education Course - mandatory for all first-time fur harvesters since 1986; final examination must be passed with a score of 90% or better. Delivered in person only; fee $65 + HST; registration through HuntNS.ca; courses usually run late summer/early fall and are managed by the Department's Hunter Education Coordinator in cooperation with the Trappers' Association of Nova Scotia (TANS). Completion gives FT (Furharvester Trained) certification; FQ (Furharvester Qualified) is the grandfathered equivalent. FQ is maintained by buying at least one Fur Harvester Stamp every four years - otherwise the course must be retaken before a licence can be issued (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 3(1A)). FT certification earned outside Nova Scotia is not transferable. An optional hands-on Trapper Education Workshop is held about once a year by TANS.
license_summary.fees: Fur Harvesters Stamp $21.17 + HST (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 3(3); 2026 Summary p. 8 - 'Fur Harvester Resident $21.17 + HST', DNR offices only). Wildlife Habitat Stamp (base licence) $5.15. Bear Snaring stamp (resident) $26.57 + HST, resident seniors 65+ $0.00; Bear Hunting stamp (resident) $26.57 + HST. Wildlife Resources Card $6.25 + HST for a new or replacement card (Department's Wildlife Resources Card page).
license_summary.harvest_report: Mandatory Fur Harvester Report: every Fur Harvester's Licence holder must submit the Fur Harvester Report Form plus fur-buyer receipt slips by April 15 (April 15, 2027 for 2026-27) - even if they did not trap. Report online at HuntNS.ca, by email (HuntNS@novascotia.ca), or on paper to a local DNR office (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 13; 2026 Summary pp. 20, 49). Failure to report carries penalties starting from $180 and loss of the opportunity to hold a licence in subsequent years. Report harvest by county, sets and trap nights; pelts retained past April 15 are registered in the report's 'Kept' column - no other permit is needed to retain furs so registered. Bear licence holders must file their information return within 2 weeks of season end (Dec 19, 2026) and submit the lower jaw or skull of any bear killed (Bear Harvesting Regulations s. 11).
license_summary.hunting_furbearers: Under a Fur Harvester's Licence, bobcat, fox, raccoon, weasel and red squirrel have hunting as well as trapping seasons (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 6(3)). Beaver, muskrat, mink and otter may NOT be taken by firearm or bow unless the animal is confined by a trap (s. 11(1)). Coyote and red squirrel are also 'other harvestable wildlife' under the General Wildlife Regulations, huntable on a base licence alone (coyote year-round; red squirrel Nov 1 - Feb 28). Raccoon night hunting requires a Raccoon Dog Night Training/Hunting Permit.
license_summary.licence_types: Fur Harvester's Licence (residents only; non-residents may not take, trap or possess fur-bearing animals except under a Non-Resident Furbuyers Licence - s. 4). Apprentice registration: a resident under 19 may set and tend traps under the immediate supervision of a licensed fur harvester 19+, identified in writing to the Department; the apprentice's harvest counts toward the supervisor's bag limit (s. 3(2)). Also relevant: Resident Bear Snaring Licence (requires FQ/FT certification) and the base licence (Wildlife Habitat Stamp) alone for 'other harvestable wildlife' hunting (coyote, red squirrel). Trapping in partnership is allowed after written notice to the Department; partners may tend traps marked with a partner's TIN (s. 11A).
license_summary.licensing_transition: Nova Scotia is modernizing licensing through the HuntNS online system (HuntNS.ca): certifications (HT, B, CT, FT, FQ, GT, N) now appear on the client's HuntNS profile, and harvest reports are filed online. Fur Harvester and Bear Snaring licences are still sold at DNR offices only (2026 Summary p. 8). No cutover date affecting the Fur Harvester's Licence was announced in the 2026 Summary.
license_summary.pelt_stamping: Otter and fisher are mandatory turn-in species in 2026-27: turn in the whole skinned carcass to the local DNR district office, exhibit the pelt for stamping, and declare your Wildlife Resources Client Number, date of capture, location of capture and method of kill (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 10; 2026 Summary pp. 21, 56). To sell an otter or fisher in the round (unskinned), first exhibit the animal at the district office and obtain a Round Permit. No furbuyer may possess a pelt required to be stamped unless it is stamped. Marten and lynx (accidental catches): entire animal must be turned in. Bear: lower jaw or full skull.
license_summary.permission: Trap setbacks (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 11(3)-(4)): no trap or snare within 274 m of a dwelling, school, playground, athletic field or place of business, or within 182 m of those places plus golf courses, woods operations, agricultural and public buildings, except as the regulation provides (owner/occupier permission, conservation-officer written authorization for nuisance trapping, and exemptions for box traps, under-ice snares, submarine traps, hooded rat traps, and - within 274 m with landowner permission - cable restraints, foot-encapsulating traps, padded modified legholds and small submerged body-grippers, which must still be 182 m from other protected places). Traps/snares are also restricted within 15 m of trails and highways (s. 11(5)-(5C); K-class roads excepted). Do not set traps on posted private forest land where the owner/occupier has posted notice prohibiting trapping (snowshoe hare snares excepted). Dens and beaver dams may not be damaged or destroyed.
license_summary.possession: Pelt possession under a Fur Harvester's Licence: beaver, otter, mink, muskrat, weasel, fisher and bobcat pelts Nov 1 - Apr 15; fox and raccoon pelts Oct 15 - Apr 15; coyote, skunk and red squirrel pelts year-round. Pelts may be kept beyond the possession date if registered in the 'Kept' column of the Fur Harvester Report (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 7; 2026 Summary pp. 55-56). An export permit from DNR is required to ship furs out of the province (not required when sold or consigned to a licensed Nova Scotia furbuyer). Bobcat, otter and bear are CITES-listed - exporting out of Canada may require a CITES Export Permit.
license_summary.quotas: No quotas in Nova Scotia. Harvest is governed by per-licence bag limits only: bobcat 5 per licence; beaver 30 per licence in Zone 1 and 20 per licence in Zones 2-4 (by the zone of the licence holder's permanent residence); bear 1 (hunting) / 2 (snaring). There is no bag limit for muskrat, fox, mink, otter, skunk, red squirrel, coyote, weasel or raccoon (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 9).
license_summary.report_violation: Report illegal hunting or trapping to a local DNR office or by phone at 1-800-565-2224 (2026 Summary cover and p. 58). Online: novascotia.ca/natr/enforcement/reportapoacher.asp.
license_summary.sunday_hunting: Sunday hunting is permitted only on designated Sundays: in 2026 the window was extended to the first Sunday immediately following October 1 through the last Sunday in December, for all harvestable species (2026 Summary p. 10). Traps may be checked and trapped animals dispatched on Sundays - a Fur Harvester's Licence holder may use a .22 calibre or smaller rimfire rifle during the fur harvesting season, including Sundays, to dispatch animals in traps (Firearm and Bow Regulations s. 7(1)). The bear snaring season expressly includes Sundays.
license_summary.trap_check: Every trap or snare designed to hold an animal alive - including cable restraints - must be examined at least once every day ('day' = 12:01 a.m. to 11:59 p.m.) (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 11(9)). Bear snares must likewise be examined at least once every day (Bear Harvesting Regulations s. 10(1B)).
license_summary.trap_marking: Since October 15, 2006, every trap or snare set for a fur-bearing animal must be clearly marked with the setter's TIN (trap identification number); the 2026 Summary directs trappers to mark their Wildlife Resources Client Number permanently on traps and snares. Exempt: traps/snares set for red squirrel, and nuisance-wildlife sets under the General Wildlife Regulations (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 11(19); 2026 Summary p. 50).
license_summary.trapping_licence: A Fur Harvester's Licence - a valid base licence (Wildlife Habitat Stamp) with a Fur Harvesters Stamp affixed - is required to trap, snare, hunt, shoot or possess any wild furbearer in Nova Scotia (Fur Harvesting Regulations ss. 2, 3). Issued only to Nova Scotia residents who are 16 or older and hold a Wildlife Resources Client Number with FQ or FT certification. Sold at DNR offices only. The licence expires on April 15 following issuance (s. 3(4)); licences can generally be purchased any time after August 1.

Bear is NOT a 'fur-bearing animal' under the Wildlife Act; it is included here because bear snaring is a certified-fur-harvester activity, paralleling the Ontario dataset's inclusion of black bear.

seasons.notes: Bear SNARING season: Oct 1 to the first Saturday of December, including Sundays (Bear Harvesting Regulations s. 6) - computed close: Sat Dec 5, 2026 (calendar-verified); matches the 2026 Summary p. 10. Resident Bear Snaring Licence required; holder must be certified as a qualified fur harvester (FQ or FT); non-residents may not snare bear (s. 4(4)). Cable foot snare only; no snare within 100 ft (30.48 m) of a common or public highway boundary; snares examined at least once every day (s. 10). Tagging on kill (s. 8); report and lower jaw/skull submission due within 2 weeks of season end - Dec 19, 2026 (s. 11; 2026 Summary p. 20). Method recorded as 'trapping' (snaring); the app method vocabulary has no separate snaring value.

species.notes: Bear gallbladders must be sealed with a permanently attached locking seal before sale or export (seal $6.22 + HST at DNR offices). species.notes: CLOSED - no open season. 'No person shall at any time take, hunt, kill, trap or snare or possess a lynx, fisher, cougar or marten' (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 6(5)); the 2026 Summary (p. 9) lists LYNX, MARTEN and FISHER as 'Closed season'. Exception: a licensed fur harvester may keep the pelt of ONE fisher taken accidentally in a trap lawfully set for another species, but the whole skinned carcass must be turned in to a DNR office and the pelt stamped (s. 6(6); s. 10; 2026 Summary pp. 9, 21, 56). Fisher is a mandatory carcass-submission species in 2026-27 for this reason. Note: the Summary's licensing section (p. 46) still lists fisher among 'harvestable furbearers' for licence purposes - the season is closed regardless.

verification.confirmation_notes: Every furbearer season date and bag limit was verified in the Fur Harvesting Regulations (N.S. Reg. 165/1987, consolidated to N.S. Reg. 25/2026, effective January 26, 2026) and cross-checked against the official 2026 Hunting and Fur Harvesting Summary of Regulations, p. 9 table - the two agree on every date and limit, including the four beaver zones. Relative dates computed and calendar-verified for 2026-27: 'last day of February' = February 28, 2027 (2027 is not a leap year); bear hunting 'second Monday of September' = September 14, 2026 and 'first Saturday of December' = December 5, 2026 (Sep 14, 2026 is a Monday; Dec 5, 2026 is a Saturday - both confirmed by calendar check and by the 2026 Summary p. 10). Coyote and red squirrel 'other harvestable wildlife' seasons and landowner take verified in the General Wildlife Regulations s. 3. Bear seasons, limits, tagging and reporting verified in the Bear Harvesting Regulations and cross-checked at 2026 Summary pp. 10, 20, 24. Closed-species statuses verified in Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 6(5) and, for lynx and American marten, the NS Endangered Species Act Categorized List (N.S. Reg. 146/2017). AIHTS adoption verified three ways: the Schedule A/B headers in the Fur Harvesting Regulations ('Certified under the Canadian Trap Certification Program'), the 2026 Summary 'Approved traps' section pointing to fur.ca/certified-traps/, and the FIC certified list itself (updated July 22, 2026), whose Note 1 names Nova Scotia as a province where exclusive use of the certified raccoon restraining traps is mandatory. Report-a-violation line 1-800-565-2224 verified on the 2026 Summary cover and p. 58.
known_gaps: Red squirrel 'other harvestable wildlife' hunting end date: the General Wildlife Regulations s. 3(2)(b) say February 28, but the 2026 Summary's table (p. 10) prints Feb 27, 2027. Feb 28, 2027 is a Sunday outside the designated Sunday-hunting window, which likely explains the Summary's print (the same table ends snowshoe hare hunting Feb 27 but hare snaring Feb 28). Modelled per the regulation (Feb 28) with the discrepancy noted in the season row; DNR confirmation is a small follow-on if the clone displays Other Harvestable Wildlife seasons.

Nova Scotia's Schedule A/B (Fur Harvesting Regulations, updated by N.S. Reg. 25/2026) vs the live FIC certified list (July 22, 2026): the lists are close but not identical - e.g., the DAM 330 appears on the FIC Phase 1 beaver killing list but not in Schedule A as consolidated. The regulation schedule is the law in Nova Scotia. A model-by-model diff is a follow-on task.
Full model-by-model transcription of Schedules A and B not done in this pass (structure and model counts only - approx. 193 models across both schedules).

Wildlife Resources Card fee ($6.25 + HST) is taken from the Department's Wildlife Resources Card page, which dates to the card's 2005-06 rollout; the 2026 Summary does not print a card fee and certifications now live on the HuntNS profile. Re-confirm the current card fee before launch.

Trap Compliance Notice wording: the 2026 Summary (p. 5) states that as of the 2028-29 trapping season only AIHTS-certified traps will be required 'for the live capture of coyotes and raccoon box traps', pointing to a Department PDF ('certified-traps-recommended-not-mandatory.pdf'). The notice's exact scope was read from the Summary PDF's text layer, which garbles some passages; re-verify the exact wording against the linked Department PDF before the clone states it as a rule. It does not affect any 2026-27 season row.

The 2026 Summary's methods-summary tables (pp. 15-18: weapon-by-weapon permissions by species) did not extract cleanly from the PDF text layer. Weapon rules in this dataset come from the Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 11 and the Firearm and Bow Regulations s. 7 instead. If the clone displays weapon tables, re-extract them from the printed booklet.

Sunday hunting: the exact list of designated Sundays for the 2026-27 season (expanded for 2026 per the Minister's message in the Summary) was not transcribed; the dataset records regulation dates with open_time null. Hunting (as distinct from trapping/tending) remains prohibited on non-designated Sundays.

Cougar protection wording rests on Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 6(5) and the Summary's 'completely protected furbearers' list; cougar is not on the NS Endangered Species Act Categorized List and its designation (if any) as 'protected wildlife' under Wildlife Act s. 49 was not separately verified in this pass.

American marten: the Department's species-at-risk page shows a mainland-population ESA listing as 'pending'. The Fur Harvesting Regulations close marten province-wide regardless of the listing's progress.

Reg. 25/2026), not the full model-by-model list. Full transcription is a defined follow-on task (see the scoping report). That check was not done in this pass.

aihts.note: Nova Scotia adopts the national AIHTS certification (the Canadian Trap Certification Program, administered by the Fur Institute of Canada) by embedding the certified lists in its own regulation as Schedule A (killing traps) and Schedule B (restraining traps) of the Fur Harvesting Regulations. The regulation schedules - not the live FIC web list - are the legal lists in Nova Scotia, and the two are close but not identical (see verification.known_gaps). The 2026 Summary's 'Approved traps' section states: 'Certain trap types must meet the requirements of the Agreement on International Humane Trapping Standards (AIHTS). Approved traps are updated periodically. Check online for an up-to-date list: fur.ca/certified-traps/.'

aihts.canada_wide: AIHTS in force in Canada since 1 June 1999 (Canada, the EU and Russia are parties; the US is not a party). FIC-certified traps mandatory per Phase 1 lists - killing traps: beaver, Canada lynx & bobcat, fisher, marten, muskrat (on land and underwater), otter, raccoon, weasels/ermine; restraining traps: beaver (cage), bobcat, Canada lynx, raccoon, wolf. Conventional steel-jawed leghold restraining traps on land are effectively banned for AIHTS species. Killing neck snares are NOT AIHTS traps and are not FIC-certified; provinces regulate snares separately. [R1 s.2a]
aihts.jurisdiction_specific: Certified coyote restraining traps and raccoon cage/box traps mandatory from 2028-29 (provincial notice). Nova Scotia is also a FIC Note 1 province for raccoon restraining traps. [R1 s.2a]

check_interval.live_holding: Daily - failing to check a snare or trap at least once every day is an offence (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 11(9)); bear snares also daily (s. 10(1)(c)).
check_interval.killing: Daily - the rule covers snares and traps generally, unlike most provinces.

canada_only.tenure: No trapline tenure - Fur Harvester Licence plus Fur Harvesters Certificate.
canada_only.trap_id_requirement: REQUIRED - every trap or snare for a fur-bearing animal must be clearly marked with the trapper's TIN (Trap Identification Number) (Fur Harvesting Regulations s. 11(19), in force since Oct 15, 2006). Exceptions: red squirrel sets and nuisance trapping; traps marked with a partner's TIN may be tended by that partner. Verified in regulation text. [R2 Item 6]
canada_only.royalty: None - the Fur Harvesting Regulations (consolidation amended to Jan 26, 2026) contain no royalty. [R2 Item 5]
canada_only.nuisance_route: Paid route exists - licensed Nuisance Wildlife Operator (defined as a person who traps/kills/frightens/excludes nuisance wildlife 'for compensation or reward'; the closest Canadian analogue to a US NWCO licence), plus a free Nuisance Wildlife Permit (Wildlife Act s. 28) issued same-day to an owner/occupier authorizing them or their agents. [R1 s.4]
canada_only.harvest_reporting_and_sealing: Hunter/fur-harvester information returns are mandatory - failing to submit is an offence. The regulations also provide for stamping of pelts. [R1 s.5]
